card_practice_desc: Work through synthetic humanitarian documents and check seeded claims against the source.

card_guide_desc: Ten common error types with synthetic examples and why they matter in humanitarian work.
limitations_body: Hints miss subtle paraphrase and reasoning errors. Models can be confidently wrong. Similarity is not truth. Nothing replaces reading the source.

debrief_dangerous_errors: Lost uncertainty, dropped caveats and scope creep are especially dangerous in humanitarian reporting. Re-read the cautious wording in the source.
debrief_false_alarms: You marked several correct claims as wrong. In practice, false alarms waste review time and can block accurate summaries.
feedback_false_alarm: False alarm: this claim matches the source; marking it wrong would slow a real review.
feedback_sources_disagree: The sources give different figures or methods. Record the disagreement and compare methods instead of picking one source.
feedback_missed_error: This claim has a seeded error you did not catch.

guide_intro: When you review an AI-written summary, check each claim that could affect a decision, a donor report or community communication. These ten error patterns appear often in humanitarian drafts.
error_wrong_number_desc: A figure in the summary does not match the source.
error_wrong_number_why: Invented or altered statistics can misdirect funding and supplies (IASC Operational Guidance on Data Responsibility, 2023).
error_wrong_date_time_desc: Timeline details are off by a day, hour or period.
error_wrong_date_time_why: Operational timing affects evacuations, distributions and coordination windows.
error_wrong_place_actor_desc: Location, site, partner or responsible actor is incorrect.
error_wrong_place_actor_why: Wrong actors undermine accountability and partner relationships (ICRC AI Policy, 2024).
error_unit_confusion_desc: Households versus individuals, or per week versus per month, are swapped.
error_unit_confusion_why: Unit errors inflate or hide needs in assessments and distribution planning.
error_not_in_source_desc: The summary adds a statement with no basis in the documents.
error_not_in_source_why: Unsupported claims can enter donor narratives without verification.
error_contradiction_desc: The claim conflicts with what the source says.
error_contradiction_why: Contradictions can reverse operational decisions, for example on disease cases or stock levels.
error_lost_uncertainty_desc: Cautious language (may, estimated) becomes certain (will, confirmed).
error_lost_uncertainty_why: Overconfidence hides data gaps that managers need for risk decisions (OCHA Data Responsibility Guidelines, 2025).
error_overgeneralization_desc: Findings from one site or sample are presented as universal.
error_overgeneralization_why: Generalization without scope can mis-target assistance across sites.
error_omitted_caveat_desc: Limits, conditions or exceptions in the source are left out.
error_omitted_caveat_why: Missing caveats can breach do-no-harm when context changes (IASC Operational Guidance, 2023).
error_invented_quotation_desc: Quoted words or attributed statements do not appear in the source.
error_invented_quotation_why: False quotes damage trust with communities and partners.
error_false_alarm_desc: Marking a correct claim as contradicted, not in source, or otherwise wrong.
error_false_alarm_why: False alarms waste reviewer time and can block accurate summaries from reaching decision-makers.
error_sources_disagree_desc: Two or more sources give different figures, timelines or methods for the same point.
error_sources_disagree_why: Picking one source without noting disagreement hides uncertainty that managers and donors need to see.
facilitator_lab_notice: This is a practice lab and human-review training environment. It is not a privacy tool, AI fact checker or safe translator.
